## Approach

Choices that no source makes are marked *planner's choice (CLAUDE.md rule 4)*. The code-reviewer confirms them at plan review. Tool behaviour known from the planner's knowledge, not from a vault source, is marked *(builder confirms)*.

### Level-1 answers recorded here (not questions)
- **What an "entry point" is in the App Router.**
  - Next.js builds separate client chunks per route. A module imported only by one route group's layout and pages reaches only that group's pages.
  - An entry point is therefore a **route group with its own `layout.tsx`**:
    - `(office)`: Projects and Settings, one entry because 11 Budgets gives them one 200 KB budget;
    - `(editor)`;
    - `(field)`: field pack;
    - `(client)`: client link.
  - `(field)` and `(client)` are the names EZD-026a's lint already covers. `(office)` and `(editor)` are *planner's choice*.
- **One root layout stays.** `app/src/app/layout.tsx` (EZD-001, EZD-010 fonts, EZD-013 service-worker registration) is not split into several root layouts.
  - Splitting it would rewrite three earlier tickets' files and tests (for example EZD-013 U3 imports `metadata` from it).
  - Rule recorded in docs instead: the root layout carries only what every entry needs. Anything else goes in a group layout.
- **"Bundle" means the JavaScript an entry downloads with no user action.**
  - This is EZD-017's Level-1 meaning of "before its lazy parts", from 11 rule 7 ("Load code on first use").
  - The field pack may load Three.js later, on its 3D tab (11 rule 7: "the phone loads Three.js only when its 3D tab is opened"). Its bundle still must not contain it.
- **Three.js itself may be in the editor's bundle; the 3D scene may not.**
  - The plan canvas is Three.js orthographic through React Three Fiber (02 Stack, 2D + 3D; EZD-207 row).
  - 11 rule 7 makes "the 3D scene" a separate chunk, not Three.js core.
  - So `three` and `@react-three/*` are allowed in editor code, and refused in Projects, Settings, the field pack, the client link and shared code.
  - The Done when ("A static Three.js import added to the Projects page fails CI") is the office case of that rule.
- **Which libraries are lazy-only:**
  - three-bvh-csg, three-gpu-pathtracer, pdf.js (`pdfjs-dist`), the DXF parser, the DXF writer;
  - the GLB and USDZ exporters (`three/examples/jsm/exporters/…`, also imported as `three/addons/exporters/…`).
  - Sources: the ticket Scope list; 11 rule 7; 02 GLB / USDZ "Three.js exporters".
- **Package names come from EZD-000's Dependencies table:** `three`, `@react-three/fiber`, `three-bvh-csg`, `three-gpu-pathtracer`, `pdfjs-dist`, `dxf-parser`, and the provisional writer (vault/plans/EZD-000.md T4). The writer stays provisional until EZD-029.
- **Where each lazy-only library may be imported statically:**
  - a lazy module (`app/src/lazy/<name>/`);
  - a Web Worker (`app/src/workers/`; 11 rule 3);
  - for pdf.js and the DXF libraries only, also background job handlers (`app/src/server/jobs/`; EZD-901a: "the browser never parses DXF text"; EZD-302 runs as a job).
  - Server code never enters a browser bundle; EZD-133's lint guards server imports from browser code.
- **The Detail editor, Sheets and the catalog drawer are lazy modules too** (Scope; 11 rule 7). Their code lives in `app/src/lazy/<name>/`, and the same rule refuses static imports into those folders from outside them.
  - Owners: EZD-702b ("The sheet renderer as its own lazy chunk"), EZD-801, EZD-1601.
- **Settings needs no lazy module.** It is its own route under `(office)` (S15 URL `/settings/users`), so Next.js already splits it per page. 11 Budgets measures it with Projects.
- **Realtime and Sentry are measured, not made lazy here.**
  - Neither `@supabase/realtime-js` nor the Sentry SDK is in the Scope list or in 11 rule 7.
  - Sentry must start before any error happens (EZD-024 Step 6: "always on").
  - Both appear by name in the bundle report on every run (Step 6), so an owning ticket sees their weight per entry before a budget fails. It can then use the lazy pattern (Step 3).
- **Real routes are not created here.** Projects (EZD-117a), Settings (EZD-103), the editor route (EZD-120b), the field pack (EZD-1404) and the client link (EZD-1202) do not exist yet, and no source fixes the field-pack or client-link URL.
  - This ticket creates the four groups, each with a layout and one **placeholder entry page** under `/dev/entry/<name>`. That path is public (EZD-007) and 404s in production (EZD-010).
  - The placeholder carries what every page of that entry will carry, so the measurement means something now.
  - Each owning ticket adds its real pages in the group and moves the measurement to its route.
- **`/` stays where it is.** EZD-007's signed-in home `app/src/app/page.tsx` is not moved, because Q-0039 may still change what `/` shows. EZD-117a creates `(office)/page.tsx` for Projects and deletes the old file in the same commit, since two pages cannot both resolve to `/` (docs, Step 8).
- **The perf check runs headless Chromium at 1600 × 1000** (EZD-017 `desktop` profile). A page downloads the same JavaScript at every viewport, so the field and client entries need no phone profile.

| `app/src/app/(office)/layout.tsx` | `office` | Projects and Settings, 200 KB | `(office)/dev/entry/office/page.tsx` → `/dev/entry/office` | `MessagesProvider` (`catalogFor('office','en')`) › `StateHost` › `<main data-entry-placeholder="office" />` | EZD-117a (`/`), EZD-103 (`/settings/…`) |
| `app/src/app/(editor)/layout.tsx` | `editor` | Editor before its lazy parts, 500 KB | `(editor)/dev/entry/editor/page.tsx` → `/dev/entry/editor` | `MessagesProvider` (office, en) › `StateHost` › `EmptyEditor` (the `/dev/shell` tree, EZD-012 Step 6) | EZD-120b |
| `app/src/app/(field)/layout.tsx` | `field` | Field pack, 200 KB | `(field)/dev/entry/field/page.tsx` → `/dev/entry/field` | `MessagesProvider` (`catalogFor('field','en')`) › `StateHost` › `<PhoneFrame>{null}</PhoneFrame>` | EZD-1404 (language per user from EZD-026b) |
| `app/src/app/(client)/layout.tsx` | `client` | Client link, 200 KB | `(client)/dev/entry/client/page.tsx` → `/dev/entry/client` | `MessagesProvider` (`catalogFor('client','en')`) › `StateHost` › `<PhoneFrame>{null}</PhoneFrame>` | EZD-1202 (also adds its path to `isPublicPath`) |

- The placeholders contain no text a user reads and no message keys, so no `es` entry is needed and Q-0030 does not block this ticket. The `(field)` and `(client)` files pass EZD-026a's literal-string lint.
- The language is `en` on every placeholder. The field placeholder does not read the user (EZD-026b, Q-0029 belong to the field pack).
- Group layouts mount no providers yet. The entry tickets move the providers and `StateHost` into their layouts, as EZD-015 says.
- The placeholders sit at different paths inside one `/dev/entry` prefix spread over four groups. Next.js allows this, because no two pages resolve to the same path *(builder confirms with `next build`)*.

### Step 3: Lazy-module pattern (builder)
- **`app/src/lib/lazy/lazy-module.ts`**: `lazyModule<T>(load: () => Promise<T>)` returns `{ load(): Promise<T>; preload(): void; peek(): T | undefined }`.
  - One promise is kept in flight; later `load()` calls return it.
  - When `load` rejects, the cache is cleared, so the next `load()` tries again. This is what EZD-015's inline error with Retry needs.
  - `preload()` starts loading and swallows a rejection, so there is no unhandled rejection. A later `load()` then retries.
  - No new dependency.
- **The rule, recorded in docs:**
  - A lazy module is a folder `app/src/lazy/<name>/`. Only files inside it import its heavy library statically.
  - Code outside the folder reaches it only by `import()`:
    - for plain modules, through `lazyModule(() => import('…/lazy/<name>'))`;
    - for React components, through `next/dynamic(() => import('…/lazy/<name>'), { ssr: false })`, **rendered only when the user opens the feature**. A dynamic component that is mounted at load downloads at load, and the contents check (Step 5) reports it.
  - `import type` from a lazy module is allowed, because types are erased.
  - `<Link>`s from the office, field and client entries into the editor use `prefetch={false}`. Next.js may otherwise download the target's code at load *(builder confirms for the pinned Next.js)*. The contents check reports that too.
- **Reserved lazy-module names** (docs table; each folder is created by its owner ticket, not here):

| Folder | Holds | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scene-3d/` | perspective 3D scene and meshes | EZD-1001a; EZD-1013 (phone viewer) reuses it or adds `phone-3d/` |
| `pathtracer/` | three-gpu-pathtracer | EZD-1105 |
| `pdf/` | pdf.js underlay | EZD-304 |
| `dxf-writer/` | DXF writer (browser use only, if any) | EZD-913 |
| `exporters/` | GLB and USDZ (or a worker in `app/src/workers/`) | EZD-1014 |
| `sheets/` | sheet renderer | EZD-702b |
| `detail-editor/` | Detail editor | EZD-801 |
| `catalog-drawer/` | catalog drawer | EZD-1601 |
| `reference/` | reference drawing in Plan | EZD-901b |

- three-bvh-csg runs in a worker (EZD-1001a), and the DXF parser runs in jobs (EZD-901a, EZD-302).
- **Proof module (dev only):**
  - `app/src/lazy/dev-sample/index.ts` exports `sampleMarker(): string`, which returns `'ezd-lazy-sample-7f3a'` (*planner's choice*, a string unique in the repo).
  - Dev page `app/src/app/dev/lazy/page.tsx` (EZD-010 pattern) renders `LazyProbe.tsx` (`'use client'`):
    - a `<button type="button" data-testid="lazy-load">` with no text;
    - an `<output data-testid="lazy-result">`.
  - On click it calls `sample.load()` (`lazyModule(() => import('../../../lazy/dev-sample'))`) and shows `sampleMarker()`.

### Step 4: Lint rule `ezdraft/import-boundaries` (`eslint-rules/import-boundaries.mjs`; registered in `eslint-rules/index.mjs`; builder)
- **Why a local rule and not `no-restricted-imports`:**
  - it needs "allowed only in these folders" per package;
  - a later flat-config block for the same files would replace `no-restricted-imports` options. That is the override trap EZD-018 Step 7 documents for its own `no-restricted-globals`, and EZD-133 is likely to use `no-restricted-imports`.
  - A plugin rule of our own cannot collide.
- **Options:** `{ rootDir, packages: HEAVY_PACKAGES, lazyRoot: LAZY_ROOT, editorCode: EDITOR_CODE, editorCodeImporters: EDITOR_CODE_IMPORTERS }`.
  - `rootDir` = the folder of `eslint.config.mjs`, computed in the config with `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`. This makes paths independent of the cwd: the app package runs `eslint .` from `app/` (EZD-001), and tests run from the root.
  - The file under lint is `path.relative(rootDir, context.filename)` in POSIX form. Prefix matching on that path avoids glob escaping for the `( )` group names, which EZD-026a's Step 4 warns about.
- **Checked nodes:**
  - `ImportDeclaration`, skipped when `importKind === 'type'` or every specifier is type-only;
  - `ExportNamedDeclaration` with a source, and `ExportAllDeclaration`, skipped when type-only;
  - `require('<literal>')`.
  - `ImportExpression` (`import()`) and TypeScript `import('x').T` types are never reported.
- **Reports:**
  1. `heavyPackage`: a bare specifier matching a `packages` entry, from a file outside that entry's allowed prefixes. The first matching entry decides.
  2. `lazyStatic`: a relative specifier that resolves (`path.posix.join(dirname, spec)`) into `app/src/lazy/<name>/` or to `app/src/lazy/<name>`, from a file not inside `app/src/lazy/<name>/`.
  3. `editorOnly`: a relative specifier that resolves into an `editorCode` prefix, from a file outside every `editorCodeImporters` prefix.
  - Message text cites 11 rule 7 and this ticket. Tests do not compare wording.
- **`eslint.config.mjs`** (EZD-001's file; one new block appended, nothing else changed):
  - `files: ['app/src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}', 'packages/*/src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,mjs}']`;
  - `ignores: ['**/*.test.*', '**/*.spec.*', '**/test-utils/**', '**/test-harness/**', '**/e2e/**']`;
  - `plugins: { ezdraft }` (the existing plugin object from EZD-026a);
  - `rules: { 'ezdraft/import-boundaries': ['error', options] }`.
  - `packages/geometry` gets no allowed place, so it can never import a heavy library. That matches 02 "no UI code", and the geometry package is imported by every entry.
- `spikes/` stays outside lint (CLAUDE.md rule 8). EZD-027's spike imports `three` freely.

### Step 5: Entry contents check (`scripts/perf/sourcemap.mjs`, `scripts/perf/js-contents.mjs`; builder)
**Source maps for the check (`app/next.config.ts`, EZD-001/013 file extended):**
- Add `productionBrowserSourceMaps: process.env.VERCEL !== '1'` (*planner's choice*).
- The gate's local build and the CI build emit `.js.map` files. Vercel builds, where `VERCEL=1`, emit none.
- So no source map is published on a deploy, whatever Q-0065 decides about the repository's visibility.
- Turbopack and webpack both honour the option *(builder confirms for the pinned Next.js; if the pinned build cannot emit browser source maps, the builder stops and the orchestrator raises a question; the builder does not switch bundlers)*.

**`sourcemap.mjs`** (Node built-ins only, no new dependency):
- `decodeVlq(str)`: Base64 VLQ as in the Source Map v3 format (ECMA-426).
- `attribute(generatedText, map)` returns `{ bytesBySource, unmapped, total }`.
  - It handles index maps with `sections`: a section applies from its offset to the next section's offset.
  - For each generated line, the UTF-8 bytes from one segment's column (UTF-16 units) up to the next segment's column, or the end of the line, go to that segment's source.
  - Bytes before the first segment, bytes after a 1-field segment, and newline characters count as `unmapped`.
  - `sourceRoot` is prefixed to each source.
- `normalizeSource(s)` returns `{ key, pkg?, subpath? }`:
  - The text after the **last** `node_modules/` gives `pkg:<name>`. A scoped name takes two segments. `subpath` is the rest. This handles pnpm's `.pnpm/<name>@<ver>/node_modules/<name>/…`.
  - Otherwise strip the known prefixes `webpack://_N_E/`, `webpack:///`, `turbopack:///[project]/`, `[project]/` and leading `./` or `../` runs. Then:
    - `app/src/<p>`, or a path that starts with `src/<p>` (webpack sources are relative to `app/`), gives `app:<p>`;
    - `packages/geometry/src/<p>` gives `geometry:<p>`;
    - anything else gives `other:<s>`.
  - The exact source forms of the pinned bundler are *(builder confirms)*. Test C3 fixes the forms listed here.
- `groupKey(key)`:
  - `pkg:*` stays as it is.
  - `app:` and `geometry:` drop the file name and keep at most two folder segments, for example `app:components/shell`, `app:lib/messages`, `app:app/(editor)`, `geometry:`.

**`js-contents.mjs`**, collector for measurements `entry-contents:<entry>`:
1. Collect the entry's scripts exactly as EZD-017 Step 6 does: fresh context, cache disabled, load plus 1,000 ms idle, no user action, the same counted set. `js-size.mjs` gains an exported `collectScripts(ctx, url)` that both collectors call; its counting rules are unchanged.
2. For each counted file, find its map:
   - the last `//# sourceMappingURL=` comment, resolved against the file URL; or
   - a `data:application/json;base64,` URL, decoded inline.
   - Maps are fetched with Node `fetch` after collection, so they are never counted as page downloads.
3. Attribute each file. Merge into `modules` (normalized key → bytes; a source referenced by at least one segment is present) and `byGroup`.
4. **Findings.** For each category in `ENTRY_RULES[entry]`:
   - `three`: a `pkg:` module matching `three` or `@react-three/`. The key is the package name.
   - `heavy`: a `pkg:` module matching a `heavy` package. For the exporters, `pkg:three` with `subpath` under `examples/jsm/exporters/`; the key is `pkg:three/examples/jsm/exporters/`.
   - `editor`: an `app:` module under an `EDITOR_CODE` prefix. The key is the matched prefix in `app:` form, for example `app:components/shell/`.
   - `lazy`: an `app:` module under `lazy/<name>/`. The key is `app:lazy/<name>/`.
   - `value` = the number of distinct `(category, key)` findings.
5. **Never pass silently** (as EZD-017 T6):
   - a counted file without a map gives `error`, with `details.missingMaps`;
   - no `app:` module across the entry gives `error`, with `details.reason: 'no app sources'`.
6. `details` holds: `url`, `files`, `forbidden` (`[{ category, key, bytes }]`), `modules`, `byGroup`, `watch` (one entry per `WATCH_PACKAGES` item, with total bytes or `null`), and `mappedBytes`, `unmappedBytes`. Bytes are minified bytes, not compressed bytes. The compressed totals stay EZD-017's `js-size:*` rows.

### Data flow
1. Gate `lint` runs `ezdraft/import-boundaries` (Done when, part 1).
2. Gate `build`: `next build` with browser source maps.
3. Gate `test:e2e` (E-tests against the harness server on 3000), then gate `perf`:
   - `run.mjs` starts `next start` on 3200 (vault/plans/EZD-017.md Step 8, moved off 3100 by plan review finding 29);
   - `js-size:*` and `entry-contents:*` load each entry in Chromium, fetch maps, attribute and evaluate;
   - it writes `latest.json`, `history.jsonl` and `bundle-report.md`, prints the report, and exits 0 or 1.

## Reviewers needed
- **code-reviewer: always.** It also confirms these planner's choices:
  - the group names `(office)` and `(editor)`;
  - the `app/src/editor/` and `app/src/lazy/` conventions;
  - the single root layout;
  - placeholder contents;
  - source maps off on Vercel (U4);
  - the sign-in contents rule;
  - the two edits to EZD-017's tests: T1(h) and T7 (Step 7).
- **calc-auditor: no.** No drafting calculations, dimensions or scaling. The numbers are counts and byte sizes.
- **ui-verifier: no.** No product screen. The placeholders are dev pages with no text that 404 in production.
- **security-reviewer: no.** No tables, auth, permissions, money, API or real share link. The `(client)` group holds only a dev placeholder; the real client-link route, its public path and its field list are EZD-1202's (03 rule 11). Source maps are not built on Vercel (U4), so no source is published.

## Risks
- **Ticket size.** This ticket is about the size of EZD-017. If it overruns, the natural split is:
  - EZD-020a: Steps 1–4 and 8 (groups, placeholders, lazy pattern, lint; L1–L9, U1–U3, U5, E5, E6). Done when, part 1.
  - EZD-020b: Steps 5–7 (source maps, contents check, report, registry; C1–C5, U4, E1–E4, E7). Done when, part 2. It depends on EZD-020a.
- **Source maps with the pinned bundler.**
  - Turbopack's and webpack's source paths and section maps may differ from C3's forms. The builder adapts `normalizeSource` to the real forms, and C3 must still pass.
  - If the pinned `next build` cannot emit browser maps, the ticket stops with a question; the builder does not switch bundlers.
  - Maps add build time and memory on the 16 GB PC (Q-0019).
  - Local sizes include one `sourceMappingURL` comment per file, a few dozen bytes, which Vercel's build does not have.
- **Budgets now gate the field and client placeholders.**
  - When this ticket is built they carry React, Next.js, Radix through `StateHost` (EZD-015) and the message helper. The Sentry SDK (EZD-024) and the service-worker registration (EZD-013) arrive later, and those tickets must keep these rows green themselves (finding 28).
  - If one is over 200,000 bytes, the builder may not shrink other tickets' code here (EZD-017 Risks). The ticket goes `blocked` with the bundle report's numbers, and the fix becomes a question for the owner's fallback (for example EZD-015's lazy Radix).
  - Q-0071 (a) fixed K = 1,000 and gzip level 6.
- **Earlier tests edited.** Step 7 changes EZD-017's T1(h) and T7. They are the only allowed edits, done by the test-author.
- **EZD-029 replace path.** The DXF names live in `eslint-rules/boundaries.mjs`, which EZD-029's plan now names (finding 11). L8 fails on any drift between the docs DXF row and the list.
- **Measurements left on placeholders.**
  - `entry-contents:*` and three `js-size:*` rows point at `/dev/entry/*` until the owner tickets repoint them (Step 6 owner text).
  - Each owner's code-reviewer checks the repoint, and EZD-1701 requires real routes.
  - The editor size stays on `/dev/shell` (EZD-017) while the editor contents check uses `/dev/entry/editor`. EZD-120b repoints both.
- **Prefetch and early-mounted dynamic components.** A `<Link>` into the editor without `prefetch={false}`, or a `next/dynamic` component mounted at load, puts code into a bundle. The contents check catches both; the lint does not.
- **Lint blind spots.**
  - Path aliases: none exist (EZD-001). A ticket that adds a tsconfig alias must teach the rule to resolve it.
  - Editor code placed outside `components/shell/` and `app/src/editor/` is not covered until the boundary list is extended.
  - Transitive imports through shared `lib/` code are caught only by the contents check.
- **Realtime weight.** `@supabase/realtime-js` is in no Phase 0 entry (only `/dev/realtime`), so its watch line reads `absent` until EZD-110 or EZD-120b imports the hub. EZD-018's hub is a static module. If the report shows an entry at risk, the owner can wrap it with `lazyModule` without changing the hub's API.
- **Client link and 3D (for EZD-1202's planner; not asked here).** S07 Entry points list a phone 3D viewer "from the field pack or client view". EZD-1202's row and 11 ("loads no editor or 3D code for sheets") say the client link carries no 3D code, and S07 Decision 10 gives the client a layout snapshot image. This ticket's checks hold under either reading, because they cover the initial download. Whether the client link may ever load 3D on demand is for Phase 12 planning.
- **`/` is outside the groups in Phase 0.** If Q-0039 is answered (a), `/` renders `EmptyEditor` without being in `(editor)`. Nothing measures `/` until EZD-117a moves Projects into `(office)`.
- **Pinned-tool details** *(builder or test-author confirms)*:
  - same-prefix pages across groups;
  - `<Link>` prefetch behaviour;
  - `productionBrowserSourceMaps` under Turbopack;
  - map source forms;
  - ESLint `context.filename` and `importKind` / `exportKind` fields on the pinned typescript-eslint parser;
  - `calculateConfigForFile` rule shape.
